Leah (AE): Heads-up — SwapKit (enterprise) wants a short POC to replace CompetitorX. Top asks: 1) wire up their existing client with minimal changes, 2) prove token billing parity, 3) complete their security appendix. Can we scope?
Ravi (SE): Quick question: do they need 1:1 HTTP surface compatibility or just payload/semantics parity? That affects adapter complexity.
Leah (AE): They said their clients call /v1/generate and expect streaming chunks + tool hooks. Minimal changes preferred.
Priya (Solutions): We can build a lightweight facade that exposes /v1/generate and translates to our API. I recommend a request/response transform that keeps headers stable for their client.
Ravi (SE): Streaming nuance: CompetitorX streams events with incremental "piece" frames and closes with an "end_of_stream" event. We stream token deltas. For parity we should implement a framing shim that converts our chunks -> "piece" events. Otherwise client-side reassembly flakes.
Priya (Solutions): Example shim snippet I sketched:
```
# pseudo
while chunk = read_stream():
  emit({"type":"piece","seq":i,"text":chunk})
on_close: emit({"type":"end_of_stream"})
```
Ravi (SE): Also watch for function/tool differences: CompetitorX returns tool outputs under `tool_result`; we return `function_output`. Adapter must map and preserve `tool_name` and `request_id`.
Jonas (Infra): POC infra ask: they want p99 latency <220ms for 32-token replies. Recommend provisional Dedicated pool in their eu-west region and sticky routing for canary. I can reserve nodes if we commit scope today.
Marta (Security): Security appendix highlights: data residency (EU only), KMS/CMK support, SSO/SCIM, IP allowlist, and a question about fallback to third-party. They also require an attestation: "no prompts stored in plaintext in hosted logs."
Alex (Legal): On fallback: they require a contractual clause that we will not forward raw request payloads to any third party without customer consent. For the POC we should propose a config flag to disable fallback.
Leah (AE): They also asked for an itemized token-cost example: convert 1000 typical requests through both platforms with real token counts and $ deltas.
Priya (Solutions): I'll run a token-diff over their sample corpus and produce a per-prompt delta table and a projected monthly cost under their traffic profile. Command I'll run in repo:
```
python -m swapkit.tools.token_delta --left competitorx-v1 --right redwood-base --in swapkit_sample.jsonl --out deltas.csv
```
Priya (Solutions): Will include a short README explaining tokenization edge cases (trailing whitespace, special separators).
Ravi (SE): We should also run an eval harness for behavioral parity. Metrics: exact match, normalized edit distance, and embedding similarity (cosine) for top response. Target: exact match >= 85% on 200 core prompts for initial pass.
Priya (Solutions): I'll produce the harness as a docker image so SwapKit can run it locally against CompetitorX or our staging.
Jonas (Infra): Canary plan I suggest: 1) facade in staging (no traffic), 2) dedicated pool + latency smoke, 3) 5% production traffic with immediate rollback trigger on error/latency/regression. I'll add tracing tags to identify POC requests.
Marta (Security): Regarding logs: hosted defaults redact prompt text, Dedicated can be configured to retain raw prompts behind CMK in their tenant. I'll prepare the exact configuration snippets and retention table.
Alex (Legal): Also they'll want to know incident escalation contacts and SLAs for the POC window. I'll draft a simple one-pager and a limited liability clause for the test.
Leah (AE): Timeline: SwapKit wants a working demo in 6 business days. Can we commit?
Jonas (Infra): Yes if scope limited to the /v1/generate surface and up to 2000 daily requests. Need final corpus and access creds today to pre-seed models.
Ravi (SE): I'll build the adapter shim and the streaming frame mapper. Will try to push a prototype by EOD.
Priya (Solutions): Token-diff and eval harness queued, I'll start runs now.
Marta (Security): Appendix answers and the config snippets by Friday EOD.
deploy-bot: provisioning: staging-swapkit created, 3x gpus reserved, logging stream enabled.
Leah (AE): Great — I'll send SwapKit a proposed scope doc and schedule a 20-min kickoff tomorrow. Thanks all :handshake:
